context.analysis:
## Overview
- An Amazon-style e-commerce Online Bookstore system for browsing, purchasing, and reviewing physical and electronic books.
- Built for global scale (1M MAU) with multi-region deployment, stringent compliance, and high availability.

## Key Elements
- Customers (End-users)
- Online Bookstore Software System
- AWS CloudFront + AWS WAF (CDN / Edge Security)
- AWS Route 53 (DNS & Latency-Based Routing)
- Identity Provider (AWS Cognito / Auth0 via OIDC)
- Payment Gateway (Stripe / PayPal via REST/TLS)
- Shipping Provider APIs (FedEx / UPS via REST/TLS)
- Email / Notification Service (AWS SES / SendGrid via SMTP/REST)

## Relationships
- Customer -> AWS CloudFront/WAF: Routes web requests via HTTPS
- AWS Route 53 -> Online Bookstore: Directs latency-based traffic across regions (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`)
- Online Bookstore -> Identity Provider: Authenticates users via OIDC/OAuth2/HTTPS
- Online Bookstore -> Payment Gateway: Processes secure tokenized transactions via REST/TLS 1.3
- Online Bookstore -> Shipping Provider APIs: Calculates rates and fulfillment via REST/TLS
- Online Bookstore -> Notification Service: Dispatches transactional emails via SMTP/REST

## Technology Stack
- AWS Global Infrastructure: Multi-region hosting (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`) for low latency and high availability
- AWS CloudFront & WAF: Edge caching and OWASP Top-10 security mitigations
- Route 53: Latency-based DNS routing with health checks for automatic failover
- AWS KMS & Secrets Manager: Region-isolated encryption keys and credential rotation
- OIDC / OAuth2: Centralized authentication supporting MFA

## Rationale
- Multi-region AWS architecture guarantees 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second global page loads for 1M MAU.
- Edge security controls, data residency enforcement, and tokenized payments ensure strict GDPR, CCPA, and PCI-DSS compliance.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
An Amazon-style online bookstore providing catalogue browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and recommendations at scale. It ensures high availability, multi-region deployment, and compliance with GDPR and CCPA.

## Key Elements
- Single Page Application (React / TypeScript)
- API Gateway / Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- Backend Containers: Catalog & Search, Order & Checkout, Engagement Service
- Data Stores: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon OpenSearch
- AWS Infrastructure: ECS Fargate, AWS S3, CloudFront, WAF, KMS, Secrets Manager, SQS/SNS

## Relationships
- Client to CloudFront/S3: HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- API Gateway to ECS Fargate: mTLS via AWS App Mesh with OAuth2.0/JWT propagation
- Backend Containers to Data Stores: TLS-encrypted TCP with AWS RDS Proxy
- Inter-service communication: Asynchronous via Amazon SQS/SNS
- External integrations: HTTPS/REST to third-party shipping and payment APIs

## Technology Stack
- Frontend: React / TypeScript hosted on AWS S3 & CloudFront for sub-2s global page loads
- Compute: Amazon ECS (Fargate) for elastic container scalability supporting 1M MAU
- Databases: Aurora PostgreSQL (multi-region transactions), DynamoDB (carts/sessions), OpenSearch (catalogue search)
- Security & DevOps: AWS WAF, KMS, Secrets Manager, App Mesh, Terraform/OpenTofu, ADOT

## Rationale
The containerized micro-service approach balances domain separation with operational manageability to handle 1M MAU. Multi-region AWS deployment with secure managed services guarantees 99.95% uptime and OWASP compliance.

Single Page Application.analysis:
## Overview
An online bookstore Single Page Application (SPA) providing catalogue browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and recommendations. Built for global scale across three AWS regions supporting 1M MAU.

## Key Elements
- Single Page Application: React / TypeScript frontend container hosted on AWS S3 and distributed via CloudFront
- Router / Shell: Component managing client-side routing, layout, and lazy loading
- Catalogue & Search View: Components for browsing, filtering, and keyword search
- Cart & Checkout Flow: Components managing shopping cart state and secure checkout
- Reviews & Ratings Widget: Components for displaying and submitting customer reviews
- Recommendation Widget: Components displaying 'Customers also bought' items
- API Client: Centralized HTTP/REST communication layer injecting correlation IDs and managing in-memory tokens

## Relationships
- Customer -> Single Page Application: Browses catalogue and interacts with UI [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Single Page Application -> API Gateway / ALB: Sends API requests via API Client [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Single Page Application -> AWS S3 / CloudFront: Serves static assets globally [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- React / TypeScript: Core framework for component-based UI development and type safety
- AWS S3 & CloudFront: Static asset hosting and global CDN with Edge functions for low-latency delivery (<2s 3G requirement)
- In-Memory State & HttpOnly Cookies: Secure token management avoiding localStorage to mitigate XSS risks

## Rationale
Client-side rendering with S3 and CloudFront guarantees sub-second global performance and high availability under 1M MAU. In-memory token storage and strict CSP headers enforce OWASP Top-10 security without introducing an extra BFF container.

API Gateway / ALB.analysis:
## Overview
[The Online Bookstore API Gateway/ALB provides secure entry, routing, and traffic management for the global e-commerce platform. It enforces strict OWASP Top-10 security, GDPR/CCPA compliance, and sub-5ms latency for 1M MAU.]

## Key Elements
- Routing & SSL Termination Proxy (AWS ALB)
- API Authentication & Authorization Filter (AWS Lambda / API Gateway)
- Rate Limiting & Throttling Module (Amazon ElastiCache Redis)
- Request Transformation & Masking Filter
- AWS WAF with AWS Managed Rules

## Relationships
- Single Page Application -> Routing & SSL Termination Proxy: Sends incoming web/API traffic [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- AWS WAF -> Routing & SSL Termination Proxy: Inspects and filters web traffic [HTTP/HTTPS]
- API Authentication & Authorization Filter -> Identity Provider: Validates JWT signatures [HTTPS]
- Routing & SSL Termination Proxy -> Request Transformation & Masking Filter: Passes raw requests [Internal HTTP/2]
- Request Transformation & Masking Filter -> Catalog & Search, Order & Checkout, Engagement Service: Forwards sanitized payloads [mTLS via AWS App Mesh]

## Technology Stack
- AWS Application Load Balancer & Amazon API Gateway: Edge routing and SSL termination
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Distributed rate limiting and throttling support
- AWS WAF: OWASP Top-10 mitigations and bot protection
- AWS App Mesh: Internal service mesh enforcing mTLS

## Rationale
- Distributed rate limiting via Redis and multi-region Route 53 failover guarantee the 99.95% availability SLA across three regions.
- Request masking and JWT validation ensure GDPR/CCPA compliance and mitigate OWASP vulnerabilities while keeping processing latency under 5ms.

Catalog & Search.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore Catalog & Search container provides scalable product browsing, keyword search, and real-time synchronization to support 1 million monthly active users. It processes high-volume read queries securely while maintaining sub-2-second page loads.

## Key Elements
*   **Catalog API Controller**: Node.js / Express component handling incoming HTTP browsing and filtering requests.
*   **Search Service Engine**: Node.js / TypeScript component executing sanitized domain queries.
*   **Caching Layer**: Amazon ElastiCache / Redis caching frequent queries and catalog metadata.
*   **Catalog Synchronization Consumer**: Node.js component processing asynchronous inventory and price updates.
*   **Amazon OpenSearch**: Managed search engine indexing catalog data.
*   **Amazon SQS / SNS**: Message bus for asynchronous event distribution.

## Relationships
*   **Catalog API Controller -> Caching Layer**: Internal Redis protocol via TCP
*   **Caching Layer -> Search Service Engine**: Fallback on cache miss via internal function calls
*   **Catalog API Controller -> Search Service Engine**: Internal function calls / gRPC
*   **Search Service Engine -> Amazon OpenSearch**: REST/HTTPS queries over TLS 1.3
*   **Message Bus -> Catalog Synchronization Consumer**: AMQP/HTTPS event consumption with payload signing (HMAC)
*   **Catalog Synchronization Consumer -> Caching Layer**: Redis pub/sub for event-driven cache invalidation

## Technology Stack
*   **Node.js / Express & TypeScript**: Core runtime for lightweight, high-throughput component execution.
*   **Amazon OpenSearch**: Scalable search engine chosen for full-text keyword search and fast filtering.
*   **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis):** In-memory cache implementing volatile-lru eviction to minimize search latency and offload OpenSearch.
*   **AWS IAM & AWS Secrets Manager:** Used for least-privilege task roles and secure Redis AUTH token rotation.

## Rationale
The component architecture uses Redis caching and OpenSearch separation to achieve high scalability and sub-2-second page loads for 1 million MAU. Security controls including TLS 1.3, IAM least-privilege, and input sanitization enforce OWASP Top-10 compliance.

Order & Checkout.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore's Order & Checkout container manages shopping carts, checkout sagas, and order processing. It uses a decomposed Spring Boot microservices architecture on AWS ECS Fargate to ensure high availability and scalability.

## Key Elements
- **Cart Manager**: Manages ephemeral shopping cart and session state
- **Checkout Orchestrator**: Coordinates payment and fulfillment workflows
- **Order Processor**: Handles persistent order state and domain events
- **Amazon DynamoDB**: Stores cart and session data
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Stores transactional order data via AWS RDS Proxy
- **Payment Gateway & Shipping Provider APIs**: External financial and logistics systems

## Relationships
- **API Gateway / ALB -> Checkout Orchestrator / Cart Manager**: Ingress requests via HTTPS / AWS Cloud Map
- **Checkout Orchestrator -> Cart Manager**: Cart item retrieval via gRPC (Protobuf over HTTP/2) with mTLS
- **Checkout Orchestrator -> Payment Gateway & Shipping Providers**: Processes payments and fulfillment via HTTPS/REST
- **Order Processor -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Persists order data via TLS-encrypted JDBC / AWS RDS Proxy
- **Cart Manager -> Amazon DynamoDB**: Reads/writes cart state via AWS SDK (TLS)
- **Order Processor -> Message Bus**: Publishes asynchronous events via AWS SQS/SNS

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: Amazon ECS Fargate for containerized Spring Boot components
- **Databases**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (ACID orders) and Amazon DynamoDB (carts/sessions)
- **Database Proxy**: AWS RDS Proxy for connection pooling and draining
- **Internal Communication**: gRPC over HTTP/2 with mTLS for low-latency cart retrieval
- **Security & Secrets**: AWS Secrets Manager, AWS IAM, and client-side tokenization for PCI-DSS compliance

## Rationale
This architecture isolates high-velocity cart operations from ACID-compliant financial transactions to protect uptime goals. Decoupling orchestration from persistence guarantees low-latency checkouts and robust third-party failure resilience.

Engagement Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Engagement Service subsystem provides customer reviews, 5-star ratings, and "Customers also bought" recommendations for the online bookstore. It uses a decoupled microservices architecture to process user interactions while maintaining compliance with GDPR and CCPA.

## Key Elements
- **Review Service:** Spring Boot (Java) container managing customer reviews and ratings (ECS Fargate).
- **Recommendation Service:** Python/FastAPI container generating book recommendations (ECS Fargate).
- **Review Component:** Handles CRUD operations and OWASP input sanitization for user reviews.
- **Recommendation Component:** Executes collaborative filtering models for product suggestions.
- **Data Layers:** Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).
- **Integration Layer:** Amazon SNS/SQS Message Bus for asynchronous event publishing.

## Relationships
- **API Gateway / ALB -> Review Service:** Routes incoming HTTP REST requests for review submissions [HTTPS / TLS 1.3].
- **API Gateway / ALB -> Recommendation Service:** Serves recommendation queries [HTTPS / TLS 1.3].
- **Review Service -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL:** Persists review data and ratings [TCP / PostgreSQL via TLS 1.3].
- **Recommendation Service -> Amazon DynamoDB / ElastiCache:** Fetches pre-computed models and caches recommendation outputs [HTTPS / Redis Protocol].
- **Review Service -> Message Bus:** Publishes `ReviewSubmitted` events to trigger recommendation updates [Amazon SNS/SQS via HTTPS].

## Technology Stack
- **Spring Boot / Java:** Selected for the Review Service to handle enterprise-grade CRUD operations securely.
- **Python / FastAPI:** Selected for the Recommendation Service for native compatibility with machine learning libraries.
- **Amazon ECS Fargate:** Provides serverless container orchestration with isolated runtime scaling.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & DynamoDB:** Store relational review data and high-speed recommendation models respectively.
- **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis):** Caches recommendation payloads to guarantee low latency.

## Rationale
Separating the JVM-based Review Service from the Python-based Recommendation Service optimizes resource allocation and security boundaries for distinct workloads. Utilizing caching and event-driven updates ensures high performance, availability, and scalability for 1 million MAU.

- Online Bookstore e-commerce platform processing physical and electronic book sales, recommendations, and reviews.

Amazon DynamoDB.analysis:
## Overview
- Internal C4 component architecture for the Amazon DynamoDB container within an AWS-hosted online bookstore.
- Provides scalable, low-latency cart and session persistence with multi-region replication and GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- Request Router & Coordinator (AWS Distributed Request Router)
- Storage Node Engine (B-tree / LSM-tree on AWS Nitro)
- Replication & Consensus Manager (AWS Multi-AZ Paxos Consensus)
- DynamoDB Streams Processor (DynamoDB Streams API)
- AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoints)
- AWS KMS (Customer Managed Keys)

## Relationships
- Order & Checkout -> Request Router & Coordinator: Executes low-latency cart operations via AWS SDK [HTTPS / TLS]
- Order & Checkout -> Request Router & Coordinator: Connects via VPC Endpoints [AWS PrivateLink]
- Request Router & Coordinator -> DynamoDB Streams Processor: Triggers change events [Internal AWS IPC / TCP]
- DynamoDB Streams Processor -> Message Bus: Publishes CDC events [HTTPS / AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables: Active-active multi-region replication across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1` for 99.95% availability.
- AWS KMS (CMK): Encryption at rest and across global table replicas for GDPR/CCPA compliance.
- DynamoDB Streams: Asynchronous change data capture for cart abandonments and analytics.
- AWS PrivateLink: Zero-trust network isolation preventing public internet exposure.

## Rationale
- Distributed consensus and auto-scaling deliver high availability and sub-second performance for 1M MAU.
- Strict IAM policies, VPC endpoints, and KMS encryption satisfy rigorous security and data privacy mandates.

Amazon OpenSearch.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a globally distributed e-commerce platform built to handle high-volume catalogue searches, secure checkouts, and personalized recommendations for 1 million monthly active users. It delivers reliable retail operations across three international AWS regions while maintaining strict GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP security standards.

## Key Elements
- **Customers**: End-users browsing books, writing reviews, and purchasing items.
- **AWS CloudFront & WAF**: Edge caching and perimeter security layer.
- **Single Page Application (SPA)**: React/TypeScript frontend hosted on AWS S3.
- **API Gateway / ALB**: Ingress routing layer using AWS ALB and API Gateway.
- **Catalog & Search**: ECS Fargate container handling product browsing and queries.
- **Amazon OpenSearch**: Managed search engine container utilizing Apache Lucene.
- **Order & Checkout**: ECS Fargate container with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and DynamoDB.
- **Engagement Service**: ECS Fargate container managing reviews and recommendations.
- **Message Bus**: Asynchronous communication via Amazon SQS and SNS.
- **External Integrations**: Third-party Payment Gateways and Shipping APIs.

## Relationships
- `Customer -> AWS CloudFront & WAF`: Accesses frontend application [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- `SPA -> API Gateway / ALB`: Sends client requests [HTTPS / REST]
- `Catalog & Search -> Amazon OpenSearch`: Queries and indexes catalogue data [HTTPS / REST via AWS SigV4]
- `Order & Checkout -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL`: Reads and writes transactional data [TLS-encrypted TCP via AWS RDS Proxy]
- `Engagement Service -> Amazon S3`: Stores automated database snapshots [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: AWS ECS Fargate for serverless container execution, ensuring rapid horizontal scaling.
- **Database**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for ACID transactions and Amazon DynamoDB for high-throughput shopping carts.
- **Search**: Amazon OpenSearch Service powered by Apache Lucene for low-latency keyword searching.
- **Security & Networking**: AWS WAF, AWS KMS for encryption at rest, and AWS SigV4 for service-to-service authentication.
- **Storage**: Amazon S3 for frontend static assets and automated disaster recovery snapshots.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages managed AWS services across multiple availability zones and regions to guarantee 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second page loads. Decoupling compute, search, and storage ensures robust scalability for 1 million MAU while enforcing strict regional data protection regulations.

Message Bus.analysis:
## Overview
An online bookstore supporting physical and electronic book sales with recommendations and reviews. The architecture utilizes an AWS-based message bus for asynchronous communication.

## Key Elements
- **Event Publisher (AWS SNS Topics):** Fan-out messaging and broadcast of domain events.
- **Event Queue (AWS SQS Queues):** Reliable, durable queuing with SQS Long Polling.
- **Schema Validator:** Application-level validation enforcing JSON schema contracts.
- **Dead-Letter Queues (AWS SQS DLQ):** Failed message isolation and storage.
- **Monitoring & Security Controls:** AWS KMS, IAM least-privilege, AWS CloudWatch, and AWS CloudTrail.

## Relationships
- Order & Checkout -> Schema Validator [HTTPS]: Validates payload structure before publishing.
- Schema Validator -> Event Publisher [AWS Internal]: Forwards validated domain events.
- Event Publisher -> Event Queue [AWS Internal]: Fans out messages.
- Event Queue -> Engagement Service [SQS Long Polling]: Consumes events asynchronously.

## Technology Stack
- **AWS SNS/SQS:** Native AWS managed messaging for scalability and 99.95% availability.
- **TLS 1.3 & AWS KMS CMK:** Encrypts data in transit and at rest for GDPR/CCPA compliance.
- **AWS IAM & SigV4:** Secures service-to-service authentication and authorization.
- **AWS CloudWatch:** Tracks queue depth and message age for performance SLAs.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures 99.95% availability and 1M MAU scalability by using decoupled, native AWS services. Strict security, validation, and monitoring protocols protect sensitive data and prevent message processing failures.
